en: An inclined plane like a ramp reduces the effort force needed to lift a heavy box by increasing the distance over which the force is applied.
Using ball bearings in a skateboard wheel reduces sliding friction by converting it into rolling friction, allowing the board to move faster with less push.
The Moon's gravitational pull causes Earth's ocean water to bulge toward it, creating high tides on the side of the planet facing the Moon.
Wrapping an insulated copper wire around an iron nail and connecting it to a battery creates an electromagnet that can pick up paperclips.
Rubbing a balloon on your hair transfers negative electrons to the balloon, causing your positively charged hair strands to repel each other and stand up.
When light travels from air into a glass of water, it slows down and bends, making a straight pencil inside look broken at the surface.
Plucking a tight, thin guitar string makes it vibrate faster than a loose, thick string, producing a higher-pitched sound wave that reaches your ear.
Heating one end of a metal spoon causes its atoms to vibrate faster and bump into neighboring atoms, transferring thermal energy to the cool handle.
Releasing a stretched rubber band converts its stored elastic potential energy into kinetic energy, causing the band to snap forward rapidly through the air.
Pushing down on the long end of a seesaw lever rotates the fulcrum, lifting a heavy load placed on the short end with less effort.
Earth's magnetic field exerts a force on a freely spinning compass needle, causing its magnetized north pole to align with the planet's magnetic south pole.
When light hits an opaque object like a wooden block, the object absorbs and reflects the light, blocking it from passing through and creating a dark shadow.
